title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction: Context: in E526 Euler treats small transverse vibrations of a uniform elastic rod (lamina/virga). The governing equation is equivalent to y_tt + (bc^4)·y_ssss = 0, with suitable constants. He separates variables in a simple harmonic mode, y = C sin(ζ + t√(2g/k)) · (α e^{s/f} + β e^{−s/f} + γ sin(s/f) + δ cos(s/f)). Here f is linked to the length k of the isochronous simple pendulum, so f^4 is proportional to k; this is the modern relation ω² ∝ λ⁴. On this page (end of Scholion 1, §13) he notes what the spatial constants still need. The end conditions of the rod fix the ratios α:β:γ:δ. Because the length EF = a enters through the second end, they also yield a transcendental equation for f, and hence for k, the frequency. Assuming forces act only at the ends, each end can be in one of three states. (I) Free end at s=0: the applied force F = 0, and the integrals ∫ds y_tt and ∫ds∫ds y_tt are normalised to vanish at s=0. The two remaining equations of §8 (moment and shear balance) then give y_ss = 0 and y_sss = 0, i.e. zero bending moment and zero shear. (II) End pinned by a stylus about which the rod turns freely: y = 0, and the moment condition gives y_ss = 0. The shear equation only yields the reaction F = +bc^4 y_sss, which does not affect the vibration (continued on the next page). (III) Clamped ('infixum', next page): y = 0 and y_s = 0. Each case supplies two conditions, so four in total. These are homogeneous linear equations in α, β, γ, δ. A nontrivial solution requires their determinant to vanish, which gives the frequency equation in f. That produces six combinations of end conditions, treated in §14 onward.

ideas.what: Boundary conditions of the Euler–Bernoulli beam at a free end: zero bending moment (y''=0) and zero shear (y'''=0)
ideas.modern_name: Free-end natural boundary conditions for the beam equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Daniel Bernoulli and Euler (1742–1744; Euler's Additamentum I to the Methodus inveniendi, E65)
ideas.where_published: E65 Additamentum de curvis elasticis (1744); revisited in E526 and analysed in Truesdell's 1960 history of flexible and elastic bodies (Opera omnia II.11)

ideas.what: Pinned (simply supported) end: y=0 and y''=0, with the support reaction given by the third derivative
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (the full systematic three-way classification appears in his 1770s–1780s vibration papers)
ideas.where_published: E526 and the related papers of the same period on the sounds of elastic rods; discussed by Truesdell

ideas.what: Four homogeneous boundary conditions determine the ratios of the constants and give a transcendental frequency equation in f, hence the length k of the equivalent simple pendulum
ideas.modern_name: Eigenvalue problem for a fourth-order ODE; characteristic (frequency) equation from a vanishing determinant

deep.surprise_reason: This is the standard classification of free, pinned and clamped ends for the vibrating beam. It is already known from Euler's own earlier work and is thoroughly documented by Truesdell. Nothing here is new to a specialist.
